table.name: conductor
table.purpose: One row per orchestra conductor, listing their name, age, nationality, and years of work; each conductor is linked one-to-one to an orchestra via Conductor_ID, with performances and shows held in related tables.

Age.name: Age
Age.description: Age of the conductor in years (range 40–63).

Conductor_ID.name: Conductor_ID
Conductor_ID.description: Primary key identifying each conductor; referenced one-to-one by orchestra.Conductor_ID, indicating each orchestra has a single conductor.

Name.name: Name
Name.description: Full name of the conductor (e.g., Antal Doráti, Charles Dutoit, Pierre Boulez).

Nationality.name: Nationality
Nationality.description: Conductor's nationality as a country code/name: USA, UK, or France.

Year_of_Work.name: Year_of_Work
Year_of_Work.description: Years of work/experience of the conductor (values 6–21, too small to be calendar years). Tentative: could also be years with the current orchestra (tenure).

table.name: orchestra
table.purpose: A reference/dimension table of 12 orchestras, each linked to a conductor (conductor table) and referenced by performance rows. For each orchestra it records its name, its conductor, the record company and physical format(s) of its major recordings, and a year value (nominally 'founded', though the 2002-2009 range suggests it actually refers to a recording or release year).

Conductor_ID.name: Conductor_ID
Conductor_ID.description: Foreign key to conductor.Conductor_ID identifying the orchestra's principal conductor (e.g. 2 = Igor Stravinsky, 8 = Pierre Boulez, 11 = Seiji Ozawa). One-to-one with the orchestra row.

Major_Record_Format.name: Major_Record_Format
Major_Record_Format.description: Physical format(s) in which the orchestra's recordings were primarily issued: CD (10 rows), CD / LP, DVD.

Orchestra.name: Orchestra
Orchestra.description: Full name of the orchestra (e.g. Chicago Symphony Orchestra, London Symphony Orchestra, Kirov Orchestra). One distinct name per row.

Orchestra_ID.name: Orchestra_ID
Orchestra_ID.description: Primary key of the orchestra table; surrogate integer identifier 1-12, referenced by performance.Orchestra_ID.

Record_Company.name: Record_Company
Record_Company.description: Name of the record label that issued the orchestra's recordings (e.g. Deutsche Grammophon, Decca Records, Columbia Masterworks); occasionally two labels combined ('Koch Records / Naxos Records').

table.name: performance
table.purpose: One row per broadcast episode/performance of a televised orchestra competition series (June run): the date, episode stage (auditions, semi-finals, live final), the featured orchestra, official viewership ratings in millions, audience share, and weekly rank. The 'Series average' row aggregates the whole series. Linked to orchestra (featured orchestra) and referenced by show.

Date.name: Date
Date.description: Broadcast date of the episode/performance, day and month only (June); year not stored. '17 June' appears twice, likely two broadcasts (e.g. results show) on the same date.

Official_ratings_(millions).name: Official_ratings_(millions)
Official_ratings_(millions).description: Official TV audience rating for the episode, in millions of viewers (range 5.2–11.58).

Orchestra_ID.name: Orchestra_ID
Orchestra_ID.description: Foreign key to orchestra.Orchestra_ID identifying the orchestra featured in this performance/episode.

Performance_ID.name: Performance_ID
Performance_ID.description: Primary key identifying the performance/episode; referenced by show.Performance_ID.

Share.name: Share
Share.description: Audience share of the episode, i.e. percentage of total TV viewers watching at that time (e.g. '28.0%').

Type.name: Type
Type.description: Stage/round of the competition for this episode, e.g. 'Auditions 1'–'Auditions 5', 'Semi-final 3', 'Live final results', 'Series average'.

Weekly_rank.name: Weekly_rank
Weekly_rank.description: The episode's weekly ranking among TV broadcasts (as text; includes 'TBC' = to be confirmed, so not purely numeric).

table.name: show
table.purpose: One row per event (match/show) in a series, recording the venue, attendance, result, and the linked performance date. The venue values (Scottish football stadiums) and attendance figures strongly suggest these are football matches rather than concerts, despite the 'show'/'performance' naming; the naming may be a disguised or repurposed schema. The table's exact real-world subject remains partly unresolved because the venue-based reading conflicts with the table and column names.

Attendance.name: Attendance
Attendance.description: Number of spectators at the event, an integer count (declared DOUBLE but all values are whole numbers), ranging 555–2431 in this sample.

If_first_show.name: Venue
If_first_show.description: Name of the venue/stadium where the event took place. All values are Scottish football grounds (St. Mirren Park, Fir Park, Glebe Park, Hampden Park), so despite the column name it appears to store the venue, not a first-show flag. The name is misleading; the values clearly indicate a location.

Performance_ID.name: Performance_ID
Performance_ID.description: Foreign key to performance.Performance_ID, identifying the date/performance this event belongs to (one-to-one). The lookup shows dates in June, consistent with a series of dated events.

Result.name: Result
Result.description: Boolean outcome of the event stored as 'T'/'F' — likely whether the home team won (or the match was won). With only two values and no further context, the exact semantics (win vs. other outcomes such as draw) cannot be confirmed.

Show_ID.name: Show_ID
Show_ID.description: Primary key of the table; unique identifier for each event/match row.
